submissions.market_view: Indexes slipped Wednesday (S&P 500 -0.2%, Dow -0.7%) as rising Treasury yields hit industrials and homebuilders, while AI-infrastructure and power names stayed bid. Samsung's record but roughly in-line Q3 profit and Korea's weak open make memory a show-me trade Thursday; stock-specific after-hours news (Wolfspeed) should drive the biggest moves.
lessons: Small-cap after-hours gaps often fade by mid-morning (NEOG opened well below its AH price and hit the stop in minutes), so on gap names set the target near the likely opening print and keep stops just under the reference close.
Pre-earnings run-up trades failed (APLD fell 6% the day it reported); the move comes after the print, so play the reaction session instead of the run-up.
Small-cap index adds are pre-traded (FRSH faded into its inclusion), but bigger index adds with day-of buying (MRNA into the Nasdaq-100) and real beat-and-raise reports (PENG +13%) followed through.

picks.thesis: Announced a conditional 30-year loan commitment of up to $1.5B from the Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital just after Wednesday's close; shares traded 19-27% higher after hours, and heavy short interest can force covering at the open.
picks.main_risk: The loan is conditional (diligence, a $750M matching contribution, warrants for up to 7.5% of equity), so a gap-and-fade below the close is possible.

picks.thesis: Fiscal Q1 crushed estimates after Wednesday's close (revenue $341.9M vs ~$116M expected, adj. loss $0.01 vs ~$0.29), after the stock fell 6% into the print; AH trades of $24.3-24.9 point to a rebound session.
picks.main_risk: GAAP loss of $221M and $6.4B debt; the stock has often closed lower after past reports.

picks.thesis: Reports fiscal Q1 before Thursday's open (consensus ~$267M revenue, ~-$0.14 to -$0.19 EPS) with the stock down ~59% this year, so a beat or a reaffirmed $68-75M EBITDA guide can squeeze it.
picks.main_risk: It has beaten only half the time over two years and tends to fade rallies; a miss sends it lower.

picks.thesis: Reports fiscal Q1 before Thursday's open after a record FY26 and a pullback to the bottom of its 20-day range; a beat or guidance raise can pop it.
picks.main_risk: Small-cap medtech; any trim to the FY27 guide gets punished.

picks.thesis: Joins the Nasdaq-100 before Friday's open, so index funds must buy at Thursday's close; it already rebounded 4.8% Wednesday and has a ~$16 daily range.
picks.main_risk: Index buying may already be pre-traded, and the earlier fear bid could keep unwinding.

picks.thesis: Beat-and-raise (FY27 ~$2.43B revenue, $4.45 EPS) drove a 13% gain Wednesday, Goldman raised its target to $85, and analysts are lifting estimates, so post-earnings drift should continue.
picks.main_risk: Already ran from ~46 to 76 in 20 days, so profit-taking could hit.

picks.thesis: DOE's conditional up-to-$4.2B nuclear loan plus the AI-power bid (Google nuclear read-through) pushed it up 3.9% on day two; it is near highs with momentum.
picks.main_risk: The loan is conditional and adds debt; power names can pull back fast with rising yields.

picks.thesis: Definitive agreements to serve Google's 2.7 GW Cheyenne data center, with Google covering costs of a $1.8B generation build, re-rate a slow utility into an AI-power name; it closed +7% Wednesday and analysts have yet to update.
picks.main_risk: Utilities rarely extend big gains, and the build may require new share sales.

picks.thesis: Samsung's preliminary Q3 operating profit hit a record ~107.4T won, confirming the memory pricing boom, and D.A. Davidson's $3,000 target lifted MU 4% Wednesday.
picks.main_risk: Samsung was only roughly in line and Korean stocks opened weak, so it could be sell-the-news.

picks.thesis: Reports Q3 before Thursday's open (consensus ~$2.30 EPS on ~$25B revenue) with the stock near its 20-day low, so a clean beat can spark a relief bounce.
picks.main_risk: Options imply only a ~3.8% move and weak volume trends or a guide cut would send it lower.

picks.thesis: Record high on AI demand: last quarter revenue $96.2B (+106%), Q3 guided to $108B, and a $150B buyback expansion.
picks.main_risk: AI capex slowdown or export restrictions.

picks.thesis: Azure grew 43% last quarter and passed $100B annual revenue, guided to ~45%, with earnings Oct 28 as the next catalyst.
picks.main_risk: Heavy AI capex pressuring free cash flow.

picks.thesis: Google Cloud revenue up 82% with a $514B backlog, TPU sales upside (Wells Fargo target $417), and Q3 results Oct 28.
picks.main_risk: Capex near $200B turning free cash flow negative, plus regulatory rulings.

picks.thesis: Custom AI chip revenue up 221% to $16.7B with Q4 AI revenue guided to $21.7B, and Anthropic set to become its largest compute customer.
picks.main_risk: Customer concentration and the risk of the $42B Anthropic financing.

picks.thesis: Steady compounder: fiscal Q3 revenue +14% to $11.6B, stablecoin card volume up nearly 200%, and earnings around Oct 26-27.
picks.main_risk: Consumer spending slowdown or interchange regulation.
